inputs.text: Cyprus is moving toward a surveillance law that would weaken judicial oversight—the kind of safeguard that matters most when state power is used against people with the least ability to challenge it. Lawyers are warning ahead of Thursday’s House vote, but this is not just a technical legal change: without independent scrutiny, surveillance can deepen existing inequalities and leave vulnerable communities especially exposed. The state should not be trusted to police itself. The bill should not be approved without real transparency and strong safeguards.
